title: Atoms For Peace | The Early Years of Nuclear Power
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: The show where you can listen to fascinating stories, and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上稀奇古怪而又美妙的事物，同时还能提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today is the start of another three-part mini-series, this time on the theme of nuclear power.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天是一档全新的三集迷你系列的开篇，本系列的主题是核能。

sentences.en: In part one, today’s episode, we are going to talk about the early years of nuclear power, how it developed side-by-side with the proliferation of nuclear weapons, and how this set the stage for what was to come.
sentences.zh: 在第一集，也就是今天的节目中，我们将探讨核能的早期发展、它如何与核武器的扩散并行发展，以及这一切是如何为未来拉开序幕的。

sentences.en: In part two, we are going to talk about the greatest disaster in the history of nuclear power: the meltdown at the Chernobyl power station.
sentences.zh: 在第二集里，我们将讨论核能历史上最大的一场灾难：切尔诺贝利核电站的堆芯熔毁。

sentences.en: And in part three, we are going to bring it all together and talk about nuclear power today, why its proponents believe it plays a key part in reducing climate change, why its critics believe it remains a dangerous red herring, and what this all means in practical terms.
sentences.zh: 而在第三集中，我们将把这些内容串联起来，探讨当今的核能、为什么支持者认为它在减少气候变化方面发挥着关键作用、为什么批评者认为它依然是一个危险的幌子，以及这一切在实际中的意义。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get right into it and talk about early nuclear power.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们马上切入正题，聊聊早期的核能。

sentences.en: On December 8th, 1953, US President Dwight Eisenhower stood before the United Nations General Assembly in New York and presented a candid truth to the delegates.
sentences.zh: 1953年12月8日，美国总统 Dwight Eisenhower 在纽约联合国大会上发表讲话，向与会代表坦诚吐露了一个事实。

sentences.en: The world had moved into the atomic age.
sentences.zh: 世界已经跨入了原子能时代。

sentences.en: Eight years before, with the detonation of the atomic bombs at Hiroshima and Nagasaki, the destructive power of atomic weapons had been clearly demonstrated to the world.
sentences.zh: 八年前，随着广岛和长崎原子弹的爆炸，原子武器的毁灭性力量已经清晰地展现在世界面前。

sentences.en: Cities destroyed in an instant, tens, if not hundreds of thousands dead.
sentences.zh: 城市瞬间被毁，成千上万甚至数十万人丧生。

sentences.en: This technology now existed, there was no way of putting it back in its box.
sentences.zh: 这项技术已经存在，再也没有办法把它塞回潘多拉魔盒了。

sentences.en: And the truth that Eisenhower presented on that day was that atomic technology had developed to such an extent since then that the bombs that were dropped on Japan would look tiny in comparison.
sentences.zh: 而 Eisenhower 在那天坦言，自那时起，原子技术的发展已经达到了这样的程度：投在日本的那几颗原子弹与之相比简直不值一提。

sentences.en: The hydrogen bomb, which was developed shortly after, was literally hundreds of times more powerful.
sentences.zh: 随后不久研制出的氢弹，威力实际上是前者的数百倍。

sentences.en: And it wasn’t just the United States that had this technology.
sentences.zh: 而且拥有这项技术的不仅仅是美国。

sentences.en: So did Britain, and so did, shock horror, the West’s archenemy the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 英国也有，而且令人大惊失色的是，西方死敌苏联也有。

sentences.en: He then set out the reality of what we now know as The Cold War.
sentences.zh: 接着，他摆出了我们现在所知的冷战的现实。

sentences.en: Countries stockpiling ever more powerful nuclear weapons and pointing them at each other, knowing full well that launching just one attack would result in a counter-attack, a huge loss of life, and very possibly an escalation that would spell destruction on a global scale.
sentences.zh: 各国囤积着威力越来越大的核武器，并将它们对准彼此，心里十分清楚，只要发动一次攻击就会招致反击、造成巨大的生命损失，并且极有可能升级为一场带来全球性毁灭的灾难。

sentences.en: But, Eisenhower pointed out, there was hope.
sentences.zh: 但 Eisenhower 指出，希望依然存在。

sentences.en: For in the destructive potential of the atomic bomb lay opportunity.
sentences.zh: 因为在原子弹的毁灭潜力中，蕴含着机遇。

sentences.en: As Eisenhower put it: "The United States knows that peaceful power from atomic energy is no dream of the future.
sentences.zh: 正如 Eisenhower 所说：“美国深知，来自原子能的和平力量绝不是未来的梦想。

sentences.en: That capability already proved is here now today."
sentences.zh: 这一已经得到证明的能力，如今就在这里。”

sentences.en: If you didn’t catch that, he said “The United States knows that peaceful power from atomic energy is no dream of the future.
sentences.zh: 如果你没听清，他说的是“美国深知，来自原子能的和平力量绝不是未来的梦想。

sentences.en: The capability, already proved, is here today.”
sentences.zh: 这一已经得到证明的能力，今天就在这里。”

sentences.en: He was, of course, talking about nuclear power.
sentences.zh: 他当然是在谈论核能。

sentences.en: Now, at the time of this speech, which would later be called the “Atoms for Peace” speech, there were no nuclear power plants, the first one would only be completed a year later.
sentences.zh: 当时，在发表后来被称为“原子能和平用途”的演讲时，还没有核电站，第一座核电站直到一年后才建成。

sentences.en: But scientists knew that generating power from nuclear sources was possible, it was a very similar principle as used when creating a nuclear weapon.
sentences.zh: 但科学家们知道，利用核原料发电是可能的，其原理与制造核武器时使用的原理非常相似。

sentences.en: As a side note, we did do a three-part mini-series on the Atomic Bomb a couple of years ago, those are episodes 284, 285 and 286, and they cover the history of the discovery of atomic energy and how it works, so I’d encourage you to listen to those if you haven’t done so already.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，我们在几年前做过一个关于原子弹的三部分迷你系列，那是第284、285和286集，它们涵盖了原子能发现的历史及其工作原理，所以我鼓励大家去听听，如果你们还没听过的话。

sentences.en: I’ll put a link in the description so you can find them easily.
sentences.zh: 我会在简介里放一个链接，这样你们就能轻松找到它们。

sentences.en: But as a brief recap of how nuclear energy is created, the chemical element Uranium is mined and then enriched, separating out an isotope called Uranium-235.
sentences.zh: 简单回顾一下核能是如何产生的，铀元素先是被开采出来，然后进行浓缩，分离出一种叫做铀-235的同位素。

sentences.en: Then, a neutron is fired at the nucleus of a Uranium-235 atom, splitting it.
sentences.zh: 接着，一个中子被发射到铀-235原子的原子核上，将其分裂。

sentences.en: This releases huge amounts of energy and results in more neutrons hitting other nuclei, and the chain reaction continues.
sentences.zh: 这会释放出巨大的能量，并导致更多的中子撞击其他原子核，连锁反应就这样持续下去。

sentences.en: Imagine a row of dominoes. When you knock over the first one, it hits the next, and so on.
sentences.zh: 想象一排多米诺骨牌。当你推倒第一块时，它会撞击下一块，以此类推。

sentences.en: In a similar way, when a neutron hits a uranium atom, it splits and releases more neutrons, triggering a chain reaction that releases enormous amounts of energy.
sentences.zh: 同理，当中子撞击铀原子时，它会分裂并释放出更多中子，从而引发释放巨大能量的连锁反应。

sentences.en: In an atomic bomb, with a large concentration of highly enriched Uranium-235, this causes a huge, destructive explosion, but if it could be done with uranium that was less enriched, then the energy given out by the reaction could be controlled and converted into usable energy.
sentences.zh: 在原子弹中，由于高度浓缩的铀-235高度集中，这会引起巨大的、具有毁灭性的爆炸，但如果使用的是浓缩程度较低的铀，那么反应释放出的能量就可以得到控制，并转化为可用的能源。

sentences.en: In practical terms, the nuclear reaction would give out large amounts of heat, which could boil water, turning it into steam, which could power turbines and generate electricity.
sentences.zh: 在实际操作中，核反应会释放出大量热量，这些热量可以把水烧开，将其变成蒸汽，从而推动涡轮机并产生电力。

sentences.en: And, ta-da, that is a very simplified version of how nuclear energy works.
sentences.zh: 然后，当当，这就是核能工作原理的一个极其简化的版本。

sentences.en: Now, back to Dwight Eisenhower. His words marked a dramatic turning point.
sentences.zh: 言归正传，回到 Dwight Eisenhower。他的话标志着一个戏剧性的转折点。

sentences.en: What had once been a source of unimaginable destruction was now a technology that could fuel cities, power industry, and even bring light to places that had never seen electricity before.
sentences.zh: 曾经带来不可想象的毁灭的力量，如今变成了一种能够为城市提供燃料、为工业提供动力、甚至能为从未见过电力的地区带来光明的技术。

sentences.en: He spoke of the need for collaboration, of bringing together the world’s brightest minds to work together on nuclear energy, and how knowledge should be shared, not kept in isolated government agencies.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了合作的必要性，谈到了将世界上最聪明的头脑汇聚在一起共同研究核能，以及知识应该共享，而不是被封锁在孤立的政府机构中。

sentences.en: A year later, he passed the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, which allowed the U.S. government to share previously secret nuclear information with private companies.
sentences.zh: 一年后，他通过了《1954年原子能法案》，允许美国政府与私营公司共享以前属于机密的核信息。

sentences.en: What’s more, it allowed for information and knowledge sharing to be global, or at least between the United States and its allies.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，它还允许信息的全球共享，或者至少在美国与其盟友之间共享。

sentences.en: The Pandora’s Box of splitting the atom had been opened, so the world should at least reap the benefits of what was inside.
sentences.zh: 分裂原子的潘多拉魔盒已经打开，所以世界至少应该收获其中的益处。

sentences.en: And it did seem revolutionary. The promise of nuclear energy was one of limitless, clean energy.
sentences.zh: 它看起来确实具有革命性。核能的承诺是无限的、清洁的能源。

sentences.en: Nuclear power stations would have no ugly black smoke coming out of the top, there would be no dusty coal trucks driving in and out of the plant every day, there would just be harmless water vapour coming out of a large chimney.
sentences.zh: 核电站顶部不会冒出难看的黑烟，没有满载灰尘的运煤卡车每天进出电厂，高大的烟囱里只会冒出无害的水蒸气。

sentences.en: They could work day and night, they needed to be built next to a river or sea or some source of water, but other than that, they could be built anywhere.
sentences.zh: 它们可以日夜运转，虽然必须建在河流、海洋或某种水源附近，但除此之外，它们可以建在任何地方。

sentences.en: And unlike coal or oil, it seemed, at least initially, that there was no limit to the amount of Uranium.
sentences.zh: 而且与煤炭或石油不同，至少在最初看来，铀的储量似乎是取之不尽的。

sentences.en: Before long, nuclear power plants had sprung up in the USSR, the UK, and the United States, and were beginning to pop up all over the developed world.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，苏联、英国和美国如雨后春笋般建起了核电站，并在整个发达世界各地涌现。

sentences.en: In 1972, the world passed 100 active nuclear reactors, most of them located in the United States, the Soviet Union, and Europe, and a year later there was a shock that would send this number climbing even higher.
sentences.zh: 1972年，全球在运核反应堆突破了100座，其中大部分位于美国、苏联和欧洲，而一年后发生的一场冲击将使这个数字飙升得更高。

sentences.en: On the 6th of October 1973, at the start of the Jewish holiday of Yom Kippur, Egypt, Syria and a coalition of Arab countries launched an attack on Israel, primarily in an attempt to regain the Sinai Peninsula, which had been captured by Israel during the Six-Day-War of 1967.
sentences.zh: 1973年10月6日，正值犹太节日赎罪日之初，埃及、叙利亚以及一个阿拉伯国家联盟对以色列发动了进攻，主要企图夺回在1967年六日战争中被以色列占领的西奈半岛。

sentences.en: Israel’s allies rallied in support, and Israel proved victorious.
sentences.zh: 以色列的盟友纷纷声援，最终以色列取得了胜利。

sentences.en: Now, why this is important in the context of nuclear energy is that in the aftermath of the Yom Kippur War, OPEC, or the Organization of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries, announced that it would impose an embargo on any country that had supported Israel in the war.
sentences.zh: 为什么这在核能的背景下很重要呢？因为在赎罪日战争之后，OPEC（即石油输出国组织）宣布对在战争中支持以色列的任何国家实施石油禁运。

sentences.en: As you may know, OPEC members are almost exclusively Muslim countries, with Venezuela being the only exception, and this organisation that effectively controlled the world’s supply of oil sought to punish countries that had supported Israel.
sentences.zh: 正如你可能知道的，OPEC成员国几乎全都是穆斯林国家，委内瑞拉是唯一的例外，这个实际上控制着世界石油供应的组织试图惩罚那些支持以色列的国家。

sentences.en: The US was the primary target, as it had sent $2.2 billion worth of arms to Israel, but several other countries were formally embargoed, meaning that they could not buy oil from any OPEC member state.
sentences.zh: 美国是首要目标，因为它向以色列运送了价值22亿美元的武器，但其他几个国家也受到了正式禁运，这意味着它们不能向任何OPEC成员国购买石油。

sentences.en: And even those that weren’t specifically targeted by the embargo felt its impact.
sentences.zh: 甚至那些没有成为禁运特定目标的国家也感受到了其带来的影响。

sentences.en: The price of oil skyrocketed, going from $2.90 a barrel before the embargo to $11.65 a barrel in January of 1974, a more than four times increase.
sentences.zh: 油价急剧飙升，从禁运前的每桶2.90美元飙升至1974年1月的每桶11.65美元，涨幅超过四倍。

sentences.en: This sudden spike in oil prices sent shockwaves through economies around the world.
sentences.zh: 油价的突然飙升给全球经济带来了巨大冲击。

sentences.en: Factories, transportation, and entire industries had been relying on cheap oil, but now costs were skyrocketing.
sentences.zh: 工厂、交通运输和整个工业都一直依赖廉价石油，但现在成本正在急剧飙升。

sentences.en: Everyday people were hit too—drivers in the United States and Europe suddenly found themselves paying double, triple the price to fill up their tanks, if they could even find petrol.
sentences.zh: 普通老百姓也受到了冲击——美国和欧洲的司机突然发现，他们的油箱加满油要支付双倍、三倍的价格，如果他们还能买到汽油的话。

sentences.en: Governments everywhere began to realise just how vulnerable they were to the whims of oil-producing nations.
sentences.zh: 各国的政府开始意识到，自己对产油国的反复无常是多么的脆弱。

sentences.en: This was really the first time many Western countries saw how deeply they depended on oil and how quickly that reliance could become a weakness.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是许多西方国家第一次看到它们对石油的依赖有多深，以及这种依赖会以多快的速度变成一种软肋。

sentences.en: In other words, energy security became of vital importance.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，能源安全变得至关重要。

sentences.en: Suddenly, the idea of an alternative energy source, one that didn’t depend on oil and seemed almost limitless, became extremely appealing.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，一种不依赖石油、且看似几乎取之不尽的替代能源的想法变得极其具有吸引力。

sentences.en: And this is where nuclear power seemed to offer an answer.
sentences.zh: 这就是核能似乎提供答案的地方。

sentences.en: Unlike coal, oil, or natural gas, uranium was not controlled by a single group of countries.
sentences.zh: 与煤炭、石油或天然气不同，铀并不受控于某一特定国家集团。

sentences.en: Nuclear reactors, if well-designed, could run almost indefinitely without interruption, providing a consistent, stable source of energy.
sentences.zh: 如果设计得当，核反应堆几乎可以无限期地连续运行，提供源源不断、稳定可靠的能源。

sentences.en: Across the Western world, governments doubled down on nuclear energy as a path to energy independence.
sentences.zh: 在整个西方世界，各国政府加倍投入核能源，将其作为通往能源独立之路。

sentences.en: France, which had been pretty much exclusively reliant on foreign oil to provide its entire energy supply before 1973, decided to launch a nuclear energy program dubbed the Messmer Plan, after the Prime Minister at the time.
sentences.zh: 法国在1973年之前几乎完全依赖外国石油来满足其全部能源供应，决定启动一项名为“梅斯默计划”（Messmer Plan，以当时的首相名字命名）的核能计划。

sentences.en: This ambitious programme set a goal of 80 nuclear plants by 1985 and a total of 170 plants by the year 2000.
sentences.zh: 这个雄心勃勃的计划设定了目标：到1985年建成80座核电站，到2000年总共建成170座核电站。

sentences.en: Now, we’ll talk more about how they did and the impact of this in part three of this mini-series, but, as you may know, in terms of meeting France’s goal of energy security and independence, it has worked.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们将在本迷你系列的第三集中详细讨论他们是如何做到的以及这带来的影响，但是，正如你可能知道的，在实现法国能源安全和独立的目标方面，它成功了。

sentences.en: France, despite having relatively low fossil fuel reserves, is the largest energy exporter in Europe.
sentences.zh: 法国尽管化石燃料储量相对较低，却是欧洲最大的能源出口国。

sentences.en: In other words, it produces more energy than it uses.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它生产的能源比消耗的还要多。

sentences.en: And this is thanks to nuclear power, which is responsible for around 70% of all French energy.
sentences.zh: 这要归功于核能，它承担了法国大约70%的能源供应。

sentences.en: Again, we’ll talk more about this in part three, and look at how the situation in France is very different to the situation in several other European countries, but the point to remember is that the 1973 oil crisis shook the French so much that it set the wheels in motion for the energy security that France enjoys today.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们会在第三集中详细讨论这一点，并看看法国的情况与欧洲其他几个国家的情况有何不同，但需要记住的一点是，1973年的石油危机给法国人带来了巨大的震动，为法国今天享有的能源安全奠定了基础。

sentences.en: In the United States, too, the government invested heavily in nuclear infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 在美国，政府同样在核基础设施上投入了巨资。

sentences.en: By the 1980s, the U.S. was starting up a new nuclear reactor every 17 days on average.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪80年代，美国平均每17天就有一座新的核反应堆投入运行。

sentences.en: It seemed as though nuclear power would indeed fulfil Eisenhower’s vision of “Atoms for Peace,” giving the world a clean and almost limitless energy source.
sentences.zh: 核能似乎确实实现了 Eisenhower “和平原子”的愿景，为世界提供了一种清洁且几乎取之不尽的能源。

sentences.en: But as the reactors went up, so did the voices of protest.
sentences.zh: 但随着核反应堆拔地而起，抗议的声音也随之高涨。

sentences.en: In West Germany, grassroots protests started to emerge, not only questioning the safety of nuclear power but also its environmental impact.
sentences.zh: 在西德，基层抗议活动开始涌现，不仅质疑核能的安全性，还质疑其对环境的影响。

sentences.en: People worried about radiation leaks, accidents, and the long-term effects of nuclear waste.
sentences.zh: 人们担心辐射泄漏、事故以及核废料的长期影响。

sentences.en: These protests would grow into a major movement and eventually lead to the formation of the German Green Party, one of the most influential environmental movements in Europe.
sentences.zh: 这些抗议活动逐渐发展成为一场重大运动，并最终促成了德国绿党的成立，这是欧洲最具影响力的环保运动之一。

sentences.en: And it wasn’t just Germany. Across the world, people were beginning to question the wisdom of building so many reactors.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是德国。世界各地的人们开始质疑建造如此多的反应堆是否明智。

sentences.en: For all its promises, nuclear energy had its risks.
sentences.zh: 尽管核能有着种种承诺，但它也伴随着风险。

sentences.en: In 1979, an incident at the Three Mile Island nuclear plant in Pennsylvania, in the United States, seemed to confirm the worst fears.
sentences.zh: 1979年，美国宾夕法尼亚州三里岛核电站发生了一起事故，似乎印证了人们最糟糕的恐惧。

sentences.en: Although there was no significant release of radiation, the partial meltdown captured global headlines and rattled public confidence in nuclear energy.
sentences.zh: 尽管没有发生大规模的辐射泄漏，但这次局部堆芯熔毁事件占据了全球各大媒体的头条，并动摇了公众对核能的信心。

sentences.en: It seemed like a disaster had been ever so narrowly averted.
sentences.zh: 这看起来就像是一场灾难被千钧一发地避免了。

sentences.en: By the 1980s, these concerns were beginning to slow down the construction of new plants, particularly in Western countries.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪80年代，这些担忧开始放缓新核电站的建设步伐，特别是在西方国家。

sentences.en: The momentum behind nuclear power had started to shift.
sentences.zh: 核电发展背后的势头开始发生转变。

sentences.en: And yet, at the same time, countries that had already invested in nuclear energy had seen its potential.
sentences.zh: 然而，与此同时，那些已经投资了核能的国家看到了它的潜力。

sentences.en: For instance, by the early 1980s, the U.S. had the world’s largest fleet of reactors, which were producing just under 20% of the country’s power.
sentences.zh: 例如，到20世纪80年代初，美国拥有世界上最大的反应堆集群，其发电量占该国总发电量的近20%。

sentences.en: Even more impressively, these reactors had become a lot more efficient and were running at nearly full capacity most of the time, which is something that few other countries had managed.
sentences.zh: 更令人印象深刻的是，这些反应堆变得更加高效，大部分时间都以接近满负荷的状态运行，这是其他少数几个国家设法做到的。

sentences.en: But, for all of the enthusiasm there might have been for nuclear energy, and the improvements in safety and productivity, in 1986 something happened that would fundamentally change public opinion: the Chernobyl disaster.
sentences.zh: 但是，尽管人们对核能充满热情，在安全性和生产力上也有所提升，1986年发生的一件事彻底改变了公众的看法：切尔诺贝利灾难。

sentences.en: Chernobyl showed the world that nuclear energy, while powerful and clean when it worked, could also be incredibly dangerous when it didn’t.
sentences.zh: 切尔诺贝利向世界表明，核能虽然在运行正常时强大而清洁，但在失控时也会极其危险。

sentences.en: The explosion and subsequent fire at the Chernobyl plant spread radiation across Europe and caused untold health, environmental, and social impacts.
sentences.zh: 切尔诺贝利电站的爆炸以及随后的火灾将辐射散播到整个欧洲，并造成了难以估量的健康、环境和社会影响。

sentences.en: It became a symbol of the dangers of nuclear energy and cast a long shadow over the nuclear industry.
sentences.zh: 它成为了核能危险的象征，并给核工业投下了长长的阴影。

sentences.en: And that, my friends, is what we have to look forward to in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 朋友们，这就是我们在下一集中将要期待的内容。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on early nuclear power.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的早期核能节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, that you've learnt something new, and if you'd never heard Dwight Eisenhower speak before, well you have now.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目很有趣，让你们学到了新东西，如果你以前从未听过 Dwight Eisenhower 的演讲，那么现在你听过了。

sentences.en: As a reminder, this was part one of a three-part mini-series on the theme of nuclear power.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，这是关于核能主题的三部分迷你系列的第集。

sentences.en: Next up we will be trawling through the rubble of the Chernobyl Disaster, and in part three we will be looking at the state of nuclear power today.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将搜寻切尔诺贝利灾难的废墟，而在第三集中，我们将审视当今核能的现状。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，大家注意安全，我们下期节目见。
